basis: First reasoned review of supplied bytes. atomscan and cleave facts ran for every original sample before and after changes. Native execution paths were disassembled with rizin and Capstone; managed method bodies, metadata tokens, delegates and async state machines were decoded with dnfile/dncil. No specimen was executed. Referenced Triage pages were unavailable through the web tool; their scores did not establish these verdicts.

samples.identification: StormAttack Active Setup loader with instruction-padding detours
samples.entry: PE32 entry VA 0x402674 calls WinMain at 0x401cb0. Configuration DWORD at 0x404120 is 3, selecting 0x401f8a -> Active Setup helper 0x401900, then self-delete helper 0x401390.
evidence: Active Setup helper creates an HKLM Installed Components GUID subkey and writes StubPath through RegSetValueExA at 0x401a4b. It reads its own executable with fopen/fread, patches a configuration and path, writes the copy with fwrite at 0x401b26, and launches it. This is unwanted login reactivation, not an ordinary installer.

Other retained configuration branches extract resource DLL/101 to the system directory (0x402460 -> 0x4023c0), replace the LanmanServer ServiceDLL value (0x401260), and inject the dropped DLL path. At 0x401150 the code creates a target process, allocates and writes remote memory, resolves kernel32 LoadLibraryA, and passes that resolved export and remote path to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.

Self-delete helper obtains its module filename, converts it to a short path, reads COMSPEC, constructs /c del with output redirected to nul, and launches the interpreter. Existing traits explicitly describe code/API profiles rather than successful installation.

Two original calls are replaced with jumps into RWX .htext: 0x401c43 -> 0x40f000 calls 0x401000 and returns to 0x401c48; 0x40190a -> 0x40f662 calls 0x401840 and returns to 0x40190f. Intervening self-moves, paired byte INC/DEC, OR and NOP runs confirm deliberate instruction padding. No encrypted code layer is needed to recover these paths.
limitations: Embedded DLL resource is 39936 bytes and identical in both native samples. Its entry RVA 0x741a points into zero bytes, import/export tables are absent, and it has no executable sections. Retained StormAttack protocol/banner text does not establish a working DDoS module.

The self-copy helper still patches historical fixed file offsets 0x6a0 and 0x3058; this rebuilt image has a different file layout. Working propagation or injection is not claimed. The original still contains the unauthorized registry-write and cleanup paths.
samples.traits: No change; four hostile and three suspicious findings retained.

samples.identification: ExtremeRansomwareBotnet .NET locker and input stealer, self-assigned namespace
samples.entry: CLR entry token 0x0600001a, Main RVA 0x2354. Plain managed metadata; no packed or encrypted code layer found.
evidence: Main calls LockWorkStation, ShowLockScreen and BlockInput(true). ShowLockScreen (RVA 0x27fc) creates a borderless, maximized, topmost ransom window with a BTC demand. Main schedules a shutdown task and repeatedly kills Task Manager and process tools.

StartKeylogger (0x06000025, RVA 0x33f0) installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL with HookCallback (RVA 0x34a8). The callback reads keyboard input with Marshal.ReadInt32 and appends timestamped key records to KEYLOG_FILE. A separate thread polls key codes 1..255 with GetAsyncKeyState & 0x8000 and appends the results every 50 ms.

ContinuousDataExfiltration MoveNext (0x060000a2, RVA 0x5500) reads key and clipboard log files and sends bounded tails to SendToC2. Sender MoveNext (0x060000a4, RVA 0x5870) serializes the incoming payload as JSON, places it in FormUrlEncodedContent, and calls HttpClient.PostAsync using C2_URL. The static initializer supplies http://cakhiatv88.wiki. This is a traced source-to-send path; no live delivery was tested.

ReadBrowserData (RVA 0x4434) copies Chrome Cookies, History and Login Data into a staging directory. StealCookies MoveNext (RVA 0x4da4) separately reads the Chrome cookie file, Base64 encodes and truncates it to 5000 characters, and calls the same sender. No browser password decryption is established.

Main calls persistence, Defender disabling, security-service stopping, hosts blocking, and UAC bypass routines. InstallPersistence writes its own path to HKCU Run, copies to Startup, and creates an onlogon task. SelfReplicate and USBWorm copy the executable to removable drives and write autorun.inf. BypassUAC writes the ms-settings command and empty DelegateExecute, then launches fodhelper.exe.

DisableSafeMode (0x0600002f, RVA 0x4120) opens HKLM SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SafeBoot writable and passes that handle to DeleteSubKeyTree for Minimal and Network. Main delegate b__9 calls this method. DisableSystemRestore additionally sets DisableSR and launches net stop srservice. DeleteShadowCopies launches vssadmin and WMIC deletion commands.

DisableDefenderPowerShell builds a Unicode Base64 command at runtime that disables real-time and behavior monitoring. Other Base64 encoding carries cookie content; the form sender uses JSON and URL encoding. Decoder guesses in cleave facts are not evidence of further code obfuscation.
limitations: RealEncryption MoveNext (0x06000081, RVA 0x2df4) targets Desktop/TestFolder, reads each file, calls EncryptAES, writes a suffixed output, then deletes the original. AES_IV is the UTF-8 encoding of H1ddenT3ars1v!!, 14 bytes. EncryptAES sets this IV before returning transformed data; the invalid IV prevents the write/delete path from completing. Existing ransomware detection accurately says replacement attempt.

The namespace, HiddenTears labels, and blackcat campaign field are self-assigned strings, not attribution to established malware families. Sample filename and sandbox score did not establish behavior.
samples.traits: Add notable SafeBoot path and registry-subtree deletion reference observations plus an admitted recovery-inhibition composite. Remove the redundant polling-dependent file-hook composite and update its nine references to the existing independent hook recorder. Other detections remain.

samples.identification: StormAttack Active Setup loader, direct-call variant
samples.entry: PE32 entry VA 0x402674 -> WinMain 0x401cb0 -> configured mode 3 -> Active Setup helper 0x401900 -> self-delete 0x401390.
evidence: Independent rizin disassembly confirms the same Active Setup registry-write, self-copy, service-DLL replacement, resource extraction and remote LoadLibrary thread paths documented for 95203f9fa8d8.

Within .text, differences from 95203f9fa8d8 are confined to the two detoured calls. This sample calls 0x401840 at 0x40190a and 0x401000 at 0x401c43 directly, has no .htext detours, and retains the same selected configuration and identical erased DLL resource.
samples.limitations: As in the other native sample, historical fixed-offset self-copy patching and the erased DLL prevent claims of working propagation or DDoS. Unauthorized persistence and cleanup code remain concrete hostile evidence.
samples.traits: No change; four hostile and one suspicious findings retained.

change_scope: All new rules use existing admitted leaf directories. Capability and path references are notable; hostile admission requires an established keylogger. New descriptions state file-scoped references, not proven handle binding or successful deletion. Consolidating the hook recorders intentionally removes an unnecessary polling requirement from consumers while retaining their other required evidence.

verification.new_controls: check.py: 10 offline positive and near-miss controls; ordinary registry cleanup has no suspicious or hostile findings, and missing recorder, deletion API, registry type or SafeBoot path prevents the new hostile finding.
verification.rescan: atomscan reran on all original samples. Both native finding sets are unchanged. Managed findings remove only the duplicate hook rule and add the three notable reference findings plus the SafeBoot recovery composite. Managed hostile count remains 17.
verification.final_gate: Run make validate after completing the review artifacts and verdict markers.
